title: A protocol for generating germ-free Heligmosomoides polygyrus bakeri larvae for gnotobiotic helminth infection studies
protocol: Extract duodenums from C57BL/6J mice infected 2–4 weeks with Hpb.
Open the infected duodenum using sterile scissors and forceps.
Carefully pick out adult Hpb worms, placing them into 20 mL of Low Antibiotic Media in a Petri dish.
Incubate overnight in antibiotic-containing media.
Wash and incubate adult worms.
Pipette the worms and media into a sterile 50 mL tube.
Complete the volume of the tube to 50 mL using sterile room temperature (20°C–25°C) PBS.
Cap and invert the tube several times.
Allow the worms to sediment by gravity for roughly 30 s, or until most worms have collected at the bottom of the tube.
Use a sterile pipette to aspirate off the supernatant above the worms.
Complete the volume of the tube to 50 mL with sterile PBS once again.
Perform this wash step a minimum of 8 times.
Pipette off all but 5 mL of media after the final wash.
Prepare a new sterile Petri Dish with 25 mL of Low Antibiotic Media.
Pipette the worms into the dish.
Incubate overnight at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 18 h.
Filter the contents of the Petri dish through a 70μm strainer into a sterile 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge the flow-through at 1000g for 4 min at 4°C.
Discard supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the eggs in 5 mL of sterile 4°C de-ionized water and transfer to a sterile 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge eggs at 700g for 2 min at 4°C.
Wash with de-ionized water 2 additional times.
Resuspend the egg pellet in 14 mL of High Antibiotic Media.
Incubate the eggs for 24 h at 4°C on an orbital shaker or horizontally to prevent pooling.
Under a biological safety cabinet, fill one sterile Erlenmeyer flask with 100 mL of LB Media and two flasks with 100 mL each of LB Supp Media.
Split a single colony from a pre-streaked plate of E. coli HA107 into half.
Inoculate one half-colony in 100 mL of LB Media using a sterile pipette tip to scrape the colony.
Inoculate the other half-colony in 100 mL of LB Supp Media using a sterile pipette tip to scrape the colony.
Use a third flask of LB Supp Media as a negative control, containing only a pipette tip.
Streak E. coli onto LB Supp Agar media from a glycerol stock.
Incubate streaked plates overnight at 37°C.
Inoculate liquid LB Supp Media with a single colony using an autoclaved pipette tip handled with sterile forceps.
Seal the inoculated flasks with autoclaved aluminum foil.
Shake the sealed flasks overnight (14–18 h) in a bacterial incubator at 250 rpm, 37°C.
Set aside two separate 10 mL aliquots of sterile LB Supp Media in 50 mL tubes and leave them at room temperature (20°C–25°C) overnight.
Centrifuge the 15 mL tube containing Hpb eggs at 1000g for 4 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and wash the eggs with a full 14 mL of sterile 4°C de-ionized water.
Centrifuge the eggs at 700g for 2 minutes.
Repeat the wash with sterile 4°C de-ionized water a minimum of 7 more times.
After the final wash, resuspend the eggs in 10 mL of sterile 4°C de-ionized water.
Pipette a minimum of five 10 μL aliquots onto a microscope slide.
Count the number of eggs per aliquot under a microscope.
Calculate the total number of eggs present in the 10 mL solution.
Centrifuge the eggs once more at 700g for 2 minutes.
Resuspend them to a concentration of 20 eggs/μL in sterile 4°C de-ionized water.
Place the resuspended eggs at 4°C while performing step 6.
Optional: Plate some eggs onto LB and YPD agar.
Incubate the plates at least 24 hours at 37°C to validate antibiotic treatment effectiveness.
Measure the OD600 of E. coli HA107 grown in LB Supp Media.
Bring a small (∼1 mL) aliquot of bacterial culture to the benchside spectrophotometer.
Use one of the two saved aliquots of LB Supp Media for the dilutions at the bench-side spectrophotometer.
Discard the used aliquot of LB Supp Media after recording OD600 values.
Do not use the opened aliquot of LB Supp Media to dilute HA107 bacteria for gnotobiotic larvae cultures.
Use the second un-opened aliquot of LB Supp Media to dilute pure E. coli HA107 down to an OD600 of 0.7–0.8.
Ensure all dilutions are performed with LB Supp Media (not regular LB Media).
In a sterile Eppendorf tube, combine 100 μL of E. coli HA107 (OD600 = 0.7–0.8) with 5000 Hpb eggs.
Calculate the required dilution of bacterial culture to achieve an OD600 of 0.740 using a spectrophotometer.
Pipette 25 μL of pure bacterial culture into the Eppendorf tube if necessary.
Add 75 μL of LB Supp Media as needed.
Pipette the egg-bacterial mixture onto nematode growth media (NGM) agar plates.
Gently rotate the plates in an orbital manner to spread the mixture in a circle, leaving a gap between the liquid and edge of the dish.
Place the seeded plates into sterile plastic bags and seal shut.
Cover these plates with aluminum foil.
Leave the plates in the dark at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 2 days.
Carefully open the bags after 2 days.
Add 1–2 mL of sterile room temperature (20°C–25°C) de-ionized water on top of the bacteria and larvae.
Re-bag the plates and leave in the dark for another 3 days.
Harvest Hpb larvae by gently pipetting sterile 4°C de-ionized water across the surface of the NGM culture plates.
Collect the larvae into a sterile 15 mL tube.
Complete the tube to 14 mL with cold sterile de-ionized water, and centrifuge at 700g for 2 minutes at 4°C.
Repeat this wash a minimum of 3 more times.
Calculate the number of viable L3 Hpb larvae by manual counting of 10 μL aliquots under a microscope.
After 4–5 days of growth, harvest gnotobiotic larval cultures.
Wash the harvested larvae.
Count and observe the larvae under a brightfield microscope.
Distinguish L3 larvae from non-infectious L1/2 larvae by their morphology, size, and movement pattern.
Plate 200 L3 larvae on LB agar plates and YPD agar plates to test sterility.
Incubate these plates at least 24 hours at 37°C.
Store HA107-grown Hpb larvae at 4°C for up to one week.
Add 50 μM of EDTA to larval suspensions prior to use to prevent sticking to the tube interior.
Recount the larvae after adding EDTA.
Keep the larvae on ice during infection.
